emails.subject: ai builder hiring at razorpay
emails.body:
Notice on your careers page that you are actively recruiting AI Builders across engineering, product, and design.

We are building MNGO to fix campus hiring, and we are onboarding our first colleges right now. Instead of guessing what recruiters need, I am reaching out directly: what breaks for your team when you try to recruit entry-level engineering talent from campuses today?

Agnesh

emails.subject: campus hiring for ai product expansion
emails.body:
As Razorpay doubles down on AI-led products and global expansion, building an early-career tech pipeline becomes critical.

In campus recruiting, most teams deal with unstructured PDF resumes, endless email threads with placement officers, and no clean way to compare candidates across different institutions. Does this match what your hiring team experiences, or is something else harder for you?

Agnesh
emails.trigger_used: Razorpay is expanding globally and doubling down on AI-led products and new software offerings for its next phase of growth.
emails.trigger_link: Expanding AI-led software offerings demands a continuous pipeline of fresh engineering talent from colleges.

emails.subject: entry-level engineering talent at razorpay
emails.body:
Following your latest funding round, I imagine scaling your technical teams is top of mind.

We are currently onboarding our first engineering colleges onto MNGO to streamline entry-level hiring. If we brought you a pre-screened, structured shortlist of final-year engineering candidates from these colleges, would you be open to looking at it?

No commitment or cost involved—just want to see if structured campus talent would be helpful.

Agnesh
